mintAuthority.summary: USDG is issuer-minted by Paxos-operated infrastructure. The Ethereum token uses a UUPS ERC1967Proxy and delegates supply control to a SupplyControl contract. Its SupplyControl owner and token defaultAdmin are an Ethereum TimelockController with a verified 24h delay. Verified deployed source and complete role-event histories through Ethereum block 26098748 establish self-administration and sole proposer, executor, and canceller EOA 0x3af3e85f4f97de7ad0f000b724fb77fe5ffc024b, with no open executor or external admin. That EOA also retains a separately verified immediate SUPPLY_CONTROLLER_MANAGER_ROLE, so the timelock does not bound ordinary issuance or controller-limit changes. Ink has a separate TimelockController and implementation; its native admin control is recorded separately, and the upgradeability object below is scoped only to Ethereum.

controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 26098748, SupplyControl owner()/defaultAdmin() and USDG defaultAdmin() returned this TimelockController; getMinDelay() returned 86400. Runtime bytecode exactly matches the verified OpenZeppelin v5.5 TimelockController source. Full RoleGranted/RoleRevoked logs from deployment block 24291710 through 26098748 contain only the constructor grants: self DEFAULT_ADMIN and EOA 0x3af3e85f4f97de7ad0f000b724fb77fe5ffc024b as proposer, executor, and canceller. Current hasRole reads confirm these memberships, no open executor, and no external admin. schedule/execute enforce delayed readiness; updateDelay is self-call-only. The same EOA's SUPPLY_CONTROLLER_MANAGER_ROLE on SupplyControl remains true and permits separate immediate controller changes, so the admin delay is not an economic issuance cap.

controls.label: USDG Ink SupplyControl owner / token defaultAdmin (separate TimelockController, 24h delay)
bypassSurfaces: Ink has its own UUPS implementation 0x1d335e8288fd65e5be3c69a25c9215b9d181be09 and default admin; the Ethereum-only upgradeability object does not attest this deployment. Current proposer/executor membership and other bypass paths are unresolved.
controls.evidence: At Ink block 57339289 on 2026-10-01, USDG supplyControl() returned 0x9a7164112029b81c07636ab7b59fa813e0883bbf. USDG defaultAdmin() and SupplyControl owner() returned this deployed contract, whose getMinDelay() returned 86400. The token EIP-1967 implementation slot returned 0x1d335e8288fd65e5be3c69a25c9215b9d181be09 and the correct admin slot was zero. These Ink addresses differ from the Ethereum upgradeability snapshot.

review.evidence: At Ethereum block 25294757: supplyControl() = 0x9a7164... (contract confirmed); SupplyControl owner() and defaultAdmin() = 0x9036566... (OZ TimelockController, 24h delay, proposer+executor = Paxos EOA 0x3Af3e85...); eth_getCode on Paxos EOA confirms no bytecode. Data drift: prior data listed the Paxos EOA as the SupplyControl owner; the TimelockController has since been interposed. All controls updated to current chain state. Supervision and reconciliation re-verified 2026-07-17: the May 2026 KPMG report documents that PDS executed a Letter of Undertaking with MAS as a condition of its Major Payment Institution licence (granted 2024-07-01) imposing prudential reserve-asset composition and safeguarding requirements, that PIE issues under a FIN-FSA Electronic Money Institution licence (2022-11-23) compliant with MiCA e-money-token requirements, and that Exhibit C reconciles redemption assets against USDG redeemable tokens outstanding at each monthly report date (2026-05-11 and 2026-05-29: assets exceeded tokens by 0.10% and 0.25%); the MAS FID record for PDS was re-checked the same day.
